knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Sealing at the marked level and storing for licensed collection is the correct route. Compressing, overfilling or using general waste all break the rule.
Some jurisdictions restrict how amalgam-restored teeth are disposed of, so the local rule is checked first. The other options are not permitted routes.
Chemical waste follows a documented route and never goes to a compacting landfill tip. The other options are not permitted routes.

practicalCriteria: Given a mock set of bags, the learner separates medical from general waste and seals one bag at the marked level without compacting it.
The learner identifies the local rule to check for a mock amalgam tooth and names the person to ask.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for the waste task
stopWorkCriteria: A bag is found compacted or overfilled and the store is not available
A chemical spill is in the waste area and no spill kit is available
